title: ILO maps GenAI exposure across Viet Nam
description: ILO applies its occupational exposure index to Viet Nam's 2024 Labour Force Survey. Around 11.5 million workers are in occupations with potentially exposed tasks, while fewer than 2% of workers are in occupations where tasks are both highly susceptible to AI and standardized.
whyItMatters: It gives a local baseline: exposure is broad, but exposure is not equivalent to full job automation.
nextWatchpoints: Whether exposed occupations show measurable employment or wage changes in Viet Nam
Whether entry-level hiring weakens faster than total employment

title: ILO reviews empirical evidence on GenAI and work
description: ILO synthesizes experiments, firm-level data, platform studies and worker surveys. It finds real but uneven productivity gains, limited large-scale displacement so far, and growing concern about inequality and younger-worker opportunities.
whyItMatters: It argues against both extremes: AI is already changing tasks, but aggregate displacement remains limited in the evidence reviewed.
nextWatchpoints: Changes in worker autonomy and job quality

title: BLS projects software developers up, programmers down
description: BLS 2025–2035 projections separate broader software development from narrower programming work. Software developer employment is projected to rise 10.2% (+174,700), while computer programmer employment is projected to decline 7.3% (-8,100).
whyItMatters: The official projection supports a task-shift thesis: routine implementation is under more pressure than broader software design and development roles.
nextWatchpoints: Actual payroll and hiring data by experience level
Whether AI exposure categories predict realized employment outcomes

title: OECD finds persistent ICT and health skill shortages
description: OECD Skills for Jobs 2026, covering 38 countries, finds persistent shortages concentrated in high-skilled occupations. ICT professionals, health professionals and teaching professionals are among the largest and most persistent shortage groups.
whyItMatters: Weakness in some AI-exposed tasks can coexist with persistent shortages of advanced technical and human-service expertise.
nextWatchpoints: Whether ICT shortages narrow as AI adoption deepens
Which specific skills remain scarce inside ICT occupations

title: IMF finds weaker demand in more AI-exposed Asian occupations
description: IMF analyzes 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies. Employer demand fell by nearly 10% in more AI-exposed occupations relative to less-exposed occupations, while the relative decline appears to have stabilized and demand for AI skills is rising.
whyItMatters: This is direct hiring-demand evidence for Asia: AI exposure is associated with weaker employer demand, but the effect is not simply accelerating in lockstep with model capability.
nextWatchpoints: Whether the relative demand gap widens again
Which AI skills command hiring premiums
Country-level results relevant to Viet Nam
